question: Does excluding the most heavily shorted names improve an existing book, on a test declared before it runs?
why_it_needs_redoing: Step 268 found cash conversion improving 11.79% to 13.92% and the sector ensemble 20.12% to 23.62%. That run does not count: six trials, undeclared, executed after seeing the underlying signal had a real information coefficient, on the same 2023-2026 window every strategy here was selected on. This is the clean version.
underlying_signal: FINRA days-to-cover, whose out-of-sample IC is -0.0435 at t=-5.30 over 2023-2026 (Step 263). The sign is negative, so excluding the most shorted is the direction the signal supports and is declared here in advance.

windows.note: the books only exist from 2023-01, and Step 261 found a structural break at 2025-04-04 inside that. Both sub-periods are reported so a result that lives entirely in one is visible.

significance: paired moving-block bootstrap on the weekly difference between filtered and unfiltered returns, 5000 draws, 13-week blocks, because the two series share almost all their holdings and an unpaired test would be far too conservative
operational_cost_declared: the screen requires a twice-monthly check against FINRA data on a book of eight to twenty-six names. Turnover created by the filter is charged at 50bps like any other turnover; the human cost of running it is not modelled and is a reason to require a real improvement rather than a marginal one.

interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_no_book_improves_significantly: S4 closes and Step 268's numbers are recorded as noise
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_improvement_exists_only_after_the_bre: reject: it lives entirely in the seventeen months Step 262 showed contain all of these strategies' performance, and cannot be distinguished from that
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_improvement_holds_in_both_sub_periods: the first verified improvement to an existing strategy in this project; it would still need forward evidence before anything changes
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.always: an improvement to a strategy that has never been proven is an improvement to nothing yet. None of these books has forward evidence.
